StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.Single, and this is the one unit in the on_stack family that goes the OTHER way: the sim does NOT override on_stack, so a second application adds. That happens to be what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236), so it is *more* faithful than the 15 units that override it to `pass` -- but it is still a gap, because C#'s AfterApplied fires only on a genuinely new power while the sim's __init__-time Minion grant (powers.py) likewise only runs on construction. Dormant: nothing reads Illusion's Amount, and the sim's stacking path (cmds.py) would not re-run __init__ anyway. Recorded so the inconsistency between this unit and its 15 siblings is visible.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): STALE, not open, and by rule 3 with the seam entry it shares a mechanism with (creature_card_cmds/step8b, closed earlier this round on the same evidence). The entry says the hook is unreachable "because an Illusion's own death takes the PREVENTION arm (powers.py `should_die` -> False)". IllusionPower HAS NO `should_die` OVERRIDE -- `'should_die' in IllusionPower.__dict__` is False, executed today. It implements `should_remove_from_combat_after_death` (IllusionPower.cs:108-114) and nothing else on the death side, so the killed creature takes the REAL arm, which is the arm that calls `_strip_powers_after_death`. EXECUTED 2026-07-29 on a real Parafright (encounter [TheObscura, Parafright]) given a player-applied Vulnerable 3 and killed: powers go ['illusion', 'minion', 'vulnerable'] -> ['illusion', 'minion'] with the corpse still in `enemies` and `is_dead` True. That is IllusionPower.cs:59-66 exactly -- the non-temporary Debuff IS stripped, the two Buffs are kept. The `is_temporary` stand-in for the absent ITemporaryPower marker is unchanged and remains the one approximation here. NOT CLOSED: nothing -- this entry carried no residue beyond the marker note.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE HOOK NOW EXISTS AND THIS POWER IMPLEMENTS IT: `hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death` is consulted by `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py, called from the real-death arm at cmds.py), and `IllusionPower.should_power_be_removed_on_death` (powers.py) reproduces IllusionPower.cs:59-66 -- keep buffs, drop non-temporary debuffs -- with `getattr(power, 'is_temporary', False)` standing in for the still-absent ITemporaryPower marker. WHAT REMAINS is that it is unreachable for the case it was written for: an Illusion's own death takes the PREVENTION arm (powers.py `should_die` -> False), which never calls `_strip_powers_after_death`. So the LIVE debuff half is unchanged -- an Eye with Teeth given Vulnerable 3 and killed still revives holding it. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py and powers.py.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# grants MinionPower 1 from AfterApplied unless the owner already has it (IllusionPower.cs:68-75, applier null, cardSource null); the sim does it in __init__ with the same `"minion" not in owner.powers` test (powers.py) and the same absent applier. The sim has no AfterApplied slot, and __init__ runs at exactly the point PowerCmd.apply creates the power (cmds.py) -- i.e. BEFORE hooks.on_power_applied rather than after, which is the only difference and is unobservable because no ported listener reacts to a Minion grant. Named per the main report's section 7 item 6: the mechanism is __init__-for-AfterApplied, and it would break for any AfterApplied body that needs the power to already be registered.

AfterDeath.maps_to: powers.py IllusionPower.on_death + should_allow_hitting + revive(), fired from the DEATH (real) arm of cmds._resolve_death (cmds.py)
AfterDeath.rationale: STALE as filed. RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: the record's premise ('powers.py still implements this via should_die returning False, so the sim takes the prevention arm') no longer matches the source. The live IllusionPower class (powers.py) has NO `should_die` override at all -- EXECUTED: `grep -rn "def should_die\\b" sts2_rl/` returns exactly 2 hits, hooks.py (the dispatcher) and potions.py (Fairy in a Bottle); zero in powers.py -- matching IllusionPower.cs, which has no ShouldDie override either (read in full: Type, StackType, ShouldPlayVfx, FollowUpStateId, ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath, AfterApplied, AfterDeath, ShouldAllowHitting, ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, AfterCombatEnd, ReviveMove). So a Parafright/Eye-with-Teeth kill runs `_resolve_death`'s DEATH arm (cmds.py) -- the REAL-death arm in C# too (CreatureCmd.cs:505-537) -- and `hooks.on_death(target, False)` fires (cmds.py), so `IllusionPower.on_death`'s `if was_removal_prevented or creature is not self.owner: return` (powers.py) sees `was_removal_prevented=False`, mirroring C#'s `if (!wasRemovalPrevented && creature == base.Owner)` (IllusionPower.cs:76-77) exactly, and both arm the revive flag (`is_reviving`/`isReviving`) unconditionally once that guard passes. `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py) is no longer skipped -- it is the death arm's own unconditional tail (cmds.py) -- and it consults `hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death`, so the buff-keep/non-temp-debuff-drop split (already separately verdicted faithful on this record's `ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath` hook) actually runs. THE REVIVE_MOVE SPLICE: C#'s `SetMoveImmediate(REVIVE_MOVE)` forces the very next turn to be the heal turn, overriding whatever the machine would otherwise have done; the sim reproduces the same observable without a state-machine splice because neither ported applier is a `MachineMonster` -- `Parafright.take_turn`/`EyeWithTeeth.take_turn` (monsters/hive/the_obscura.py, monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py) check `illusion.is_reviving` FIRST, before any normal-move logic, and `current_intent` does the same, so the flag flip inside `on_death` (executed synchronously, before the caller returns) is visible immediately and forces the heal turn exactly as `SetMoveImmediate` does. `ShouldAllowHitting` (powers.py) matches IllusionPower.cs:96-104 (`creature != base.Owner -> true; else !IsReviving`) line for line, so the reviving owner is untargetable in both engines. `revive()` (powers.py) reproduces `ReviveMove`'s `Heal(MaxHp - CurrentHp)` (IllusionPower.cs:127); the two remaining ReviveMove statements (`TriggerAnim WakeUpTrigger`, the Parafright SFX) are presentation, already separately waived on this record. EXECUTED AND PINNED: test/test_hive.py::TestTheObscura::test_parafright_revives_instead_of_dying -- kills a live Parafright with 999 damage, asserts `illusion.is_reviving`, `current_intent.move_type == HEAL`, unhittable (`DamageCmd.deal(...) == 0`), and after `end_turn()` the creature is at full HP with `is_reviving` cleared. SECOND EXECUTED WITNESS (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-2-illusion-death.py`): an EyeWithTeeth given non-temporary Vulnerable(2) and killed with 999 damage ends `is_dead=True, hp=0, retained_after_death=True`, powers `['illusion','minion','vulnerable']` -> `['illusion','minion']` (the debuff stripped, the buffs kept, matching `should_power_be_removed_on_death`), `is_reviving=True`. VERIFIED by reading powers.py, cmds.py, monsters/hive/the_obscura.py and monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py in full, and src/Core/Models/Powers/IllusionPower.cs in full.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: powers.py IllusionPower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death, consulted at cmds.py on the death arm
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.rationale: STALE as filed. Settled independently of the AfterDeath entry above by executing this witness itself, not by inheriting its label: the premise ('this power still does not implement should_remove_from_combat_after_death, because it reaches retention through should_die instead') is false. `IllusionPower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death` (powers.py) reads `return creature is not self.owner`, which is `ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` (IllusionPower.cs:106-113: `if (creature != base.Owner) return true; return false;`) read line for line, and the power's own comment now says so explicitly: 'This is the ONLY death-side predicate the power implements -- it has no ShouldDie override at all, so the death is REAL and only the removal is refused.' It is genuinely consulted: `_resolve_death`'s death arm sets `target.retained_after_death = not hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death(target)` (cmds.py), the sim's port of `Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` gating `shouldRemoveFromCombat` at CreatureCmd.cs:507. So the reviving creature IS retained via this hook, not via an unconditional prevention-arm flag as the stale text claimed -- the prevention arm is not even reached (see the AfterDeath entry and guard g6). VERIFIED by reading powers.py and cmds.py together.
